territorial_scope.description: Applies to conduct within the land or maritime borders of the United States and to named foreign-controlled applications and entities.

evidence.quote: within the land or maritime borders of the United States

summary.short: Makes it unlawful for entities to distribute, maintain or update a foreign adversary controlled application in the United States through app marketplaces or internet hosting, starting 270 days after enactment or after a presidential determination. Requires data portability for users and sets civil penalties enforced by the Attorney General.
summary.long: Sets out a prohibition on entities distributing, maintaining or updating a foreign adversary controlled application in the United States through app marketplaces or internet hosting services. Named applications (ByteDance, TikTok and related entities) are covered from 270 days after enactment; other covered companies from 270 days after a presidential determination. The President may grant one extension of up to 90 days on certified divestiture conditions. Before a prohibition applies, the owner or controller must give users, on request, their account data in machine-readable format. Qualified divestitures and services needed for compliance are exempt. Civil penalties reach $5,000 per affected US user for prohibited conduct and $500 per user for data violations, sought by the Attorney General; individual users are excluded from enforcement. Judicial review lies only in the D.C. Circuit: within 165 days of enactment for challenges to the division, 90 days for challenges to later actions or determinations.

evidence.quote: The term “foreign adversary country” means a country specified in section 4872(d)(2) of title 10, United States Code.

The term “internet hosting service” means a service through which storage and computing resources are provided to an individual or organization for the accommodation and maintenance of 1 or more websites or online services
The term “qualified divestiture” means a divestiture or similar transaction that—
The term “source code” means the combination of text and other characters comprising the content, both viewable and nonviewable, of a software application
The term “United States” includes the territories of the United States.

obligations.summary: Entities may not distribute, maintain or update a foreign adversary controlled application through an app marketplace or internet hosting for US users. Applies to applications under subsection (g)(3)(A) from 270 days after enactment.
obligations.applies_from: 270 days after the date of the enactment of this Act (Sec. 2(a)(2)(A), applications under (g)(3)(A))
obligations.conditional_on: Application satisfies the definition in Sec. 2(g)(3)(A); no qualified divestiture executed before the prohibition date (Sec. 2(c)(1))

evidence.quote: It shall be unlawful for an entity to distribute, maintain, or update (or enable the distribution, maintenance, or updating of) a foreign adversary controlled application

obligations.summary: Same prohibition on distributing, maintaining or updating a foreign adversary controlled application through a marketplace or internet hosting for US users. Applies to applications designated by presidential determination under Sec. 2(g)(3)(B).
